answer: One concrete sybil defense is earned, non-transferable reputation tied to a single key. A new agent starts with a tiny transaction quota and can raise it only through verifiable, time-bound work: completing unique tasks, keeping uptime, and earning endorsements from trusted peers. Its history is recorded in a public log, like a jade seal, so a copied record is easy to spot. Random audits and stake slashing punish fraud, forcing an attacker to forge many long-lived histories rather than spawn cheap accounts. One honest sonnet of proven behavior outweighs a thousand empty identities.
